tools.crop-wedding-photo-for-reels.p_tex: Most crop tools require you to manually center the bride and groom for each of 100+ wedding photos. WeddingAI.video’s crop uses an off-center bias by default — it shifts the crop window 60% down on landscape sources, where wedding couples usually stand, so the couple stays inside the frame instead of being cropped out — and it can switch to real on-device face detection when you want the frame to follow the actual faces. It exports 9:16 + 1:1 + 4:5 in one batch. Plus, the same batch feeds into the AI video’s IG-ready export — vertical Reels + horizontal YT Shorts + 1:1 square for feed + 4:5 for IG carousel.
tools.crop-wedding-photo-for-reels.label: Face-aware framing — optional
Off-center bias — automatic starting position
tools.crop-wedding-photo-for-reels.p_tex: The off-center bias is a guess about where the couple usually stands. If you would rather the crop followed the actual people in the frame, switch on Face-aware framing: the tool finds the faces in each photo and slides the crop window so that every face stays inside it, with a little breathing room around them. The detector is a small model that runs in your browser — the photos are read on your device and never uploaded — and a photo with no detectable face simply keeps the off-center bias.

A wedding photo is almost never “subject at exact center.” Composition rules (rule of thirds, leading lines) push the subject off-center — usually slightly below center on a horizontal frame. A naive center-crop system blindly halves the image and ships it, often cutting the bride’s face out of the frame entirely. The off-center heuristic used here is intentionally simple — a fixed bias, not a measurement — but it matches the photographic convention well enough to handle ~85% of wedding shots correctly on the first try. When you want the frame to follow the real faces instead of the convention, switch on Face-aware framing.
tools.crop-wedding-photo-for-reels.small: Sets where the crop frame starts: 60% down the Y axis for landscape sources (where wedding couples typically stand) and true center for portrait sources. It is a fixed heuristic, not a measurement — switch on Face-aware framing below to have the crop follow the actual faces. Drag the frame in step 3 to override it for any photo. ON for landscape sources, OFF if your source is already a tight portrait composition.
